root_cause.text: In the e1000/e1000e TX DMA mapping error path, `count` already represented the exact number of successfully mapped buffers, but the cleanup code decremented `count` before unmapping, causing an off-by-one bug that skipped unmapping one DMA-mapped buffer and leaked it.
root_cause.evidence: The patch removes `if (count) count--;` immediately before `while (count--)` in both `drivers/net/ethernet/intel/e1000/e1000_main.c` and `drivers/net/ethernet/intel/e1000e/netdev.c`, and the CVE/commit message explicitly states that “count is incremented after a successful mapping” so pre-decrementing it “causes an off-by-one error” where “exactly one DMA mapping would leak.”

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix the TX DMA mapping error path to clean up all mapped buffers instead of skipping one entry before the unmap loop.
intent_record.what: The change removes the two-line conditional block `if (count) count--;` from the `dma_error:` path in `e1000_tx_map()`, leaving the subsequent `while (count--)` cleanup loop unchanged.
intent_record.how: On TX DMA mapping failure, the error-handling path no longer decrements `count` before entering the cleanup loop, so cleanup now iterates over the full number of previously mapped entries instead of skipping one when `count` is nonzero. This fixes incomplete unmapping or cleanup of mapped transmit buffers during the failure path.
